title: Your first IPv6 LAN
summary: Assign a workstation its first IPv6 address and test local communication.
description: The cables and switch are ready. Reference host uses 2001:db8:41::20/64. Configure Workstation eth0 as 2001:db8:41::10/64, then ping the reference host. This is one LAN; leave the IPv6 gateway empty. Use Configure device > IPv6.
hints: IPv6 addresses and prefix lengths are configured separately.
Hosts in the same IPv6 /64 do not need a gateway to communicate.

title: Repair an IPv6 prefix
summary: Find why two IPv6 hosts on the same cable cannot communicate.
description: Both addresses belong to 2001:db8:42::/64, but Workstation has an incorrect prefix length. Keep its address 2001:db8:42::10 and repair eth0 to /64. Reference host is locked at 2001:db8:42:0:8000::20/64. Do not add a gateway or change cables.
hints: The prefix decides which addresses are directly reachable.
Compare the first 64 bits rather than the number of visible groups in the compressed notation.

title: Choose an IPv6 gateway
summary: Reach a second IPv6 LAN without disturbing working IPv4 connectivity.
description: Client can already reach Training server at 192.168.44.80 over IPv4. IPv6 fails because Client has no IPv6 default gateway. Keep Client at 2001:db8:43::10/64 and set its IPv6 gateway to Gateway eth0, 2001:db8:43::1. Reach Training server at 2001:db8:44::80 and preserve IPv4 connectivity. The router and server are locked.
hints: An IPv6 gateway must be reachable on the client LAN.
The IPv4 and IPv6 gateway fields are independent.

title: Permit the training portal
summary: Allow HTTP through an inbound ACL while other tested traffic stays blocked.
description: Gateway has an empty IPv4 ACL named WEB_ONLY applied inbound on eth0. Empty ACLs deny everything. Add a permit rule for TCP from 192.168.45.0/24 to 192.168.46.80, destination port 80. Leave other traffic denied: Client must not reach TCP 22, UDP 53 or ping on the server. Keep WEB_ONLY bound inbound on eth0. The return path uses eth1 inbound and eth0 outbound, where no ACL is bound. Use the HTTP tool to verify the portal.
hints: The first matching rule wins; an ACL ends with an implicit deny.
HTTP uses TCP destination port 80. This inbound ACL is only on the client-facing interface.

title: Isolate the guest subnet
summary: Apply an existing ACL in the right place to protect an internal server.
description: STAFF_ONLY already contains an ordered deny for source 192.168.48.0/24 to destination 192.168.49.0/24, followed by permit ip any any. It is not applied to any interface. Bind this IPv4 ACL outbound on Department router eth2, toward Internal server. Staff must retain ping, TCP 80 and UDP 53 access to 192.168.49.80. Guest must lose those paths but must still reach its own gateway at 192.168.48.1. Keep all interface addresses.
hints: Outbound on eth2 checks packets leaving the router toward the server LAN.
The final permit keeps unrelated traffic working.

title: Form your first OSPF neighbor
summary: Enable OSPF on a prepared router and learn a remote LAN.
description: West router is ready for OSPF area 0. East router has router ID 2.2.2.2 and interface entries prepared, but OSPF is disabled. Enable it without adding static routes. Keep eth1 non-passive for the transit link and eth0 passive for the server LAN. West router must form a Full neighbor with East router, learn 192.168.51.0/24 via 10.50.0.2 on eth1, and allow West client to reach East server. Inspect West router to see the learned route.
hints: Enabling a prepared OSPF process starts neighbor discovery on non-passive interfaces.
Passive LAN interfaces advertise their network without forming neighbors with PCs.

title: Repair a dual-stack transit path
summary: Restore IPv6 static routing across three routers while preserving IPv4.
description: IPv4 is working across all three routers. IPv6 fails: West router lacks the route to 2001:db8:53::/64; Transit router lacks the return route to 2001:db8:52::/64; East router has IPv6 forwarding disabled. On West router add 2001:db8:53::/64 via 2001:db8:1252::2 on eth1. On Transit router add 2001:db8:52::/64 via 2001:db8:1252::1 on eth0. Enable IPv6 forwarding on East router. Keep existing routes and verify both directions between the two end devices, including IPv4.
hints: A request and its reply can fail on different routers.
IPv6 forwarding is separate from IPv4 routing.

title: Repair rule order and the reply path
summary: Fix two independent ACL mistakes to serve HTTP without opening other ports.
description: REQUESTS is inbound on Gateway eth0, but its deny-all rule is above its HTTP permit. Reorder it so TCP destination port 80 from 192.168.54.0/24 to 192.168.55.80 is allowed first. REPLIES is inbound on eth1 and incorrectly checks destination port 80; a server reply uses source port 80. Repair that permit for source 192.168.55.80 and destination 192.168.54.0/24, before its deny-all. Keep both bindings and keep TCP 22, UDP 53 and ICMP blocked. ACLs are stateless. Use HTTP and the packet trace to verify the request and reply.
hints: A later permit is never reached if an earlier deny already matches.
The reply swaps source and destination ports: TCP 80 becomes the source port.

title: Repair an area and a missing network
summary: Restore dynamic routing across three routers without substituting static routes.
description: The intended design is OSPF area 0 on every router. Core router was set to area 1, so neither transit adjacency can form. Datacenter router also omits eth1 from its advertised interfaces. Set Core router to area 0; on Datacenter router advertise eth1 as passive with cost 10. Keep transit interfaces non-passive and retain all existing advertisements. Branch router must learn 192.168.57.0/24 through OSPF via 10.56.0.2 on eth1; Datacenter router must learn 192.168.56.0/24 via 10.57.0.1 on eth0. Verify end-to-end communication.
hints: Use the device inspector to distinguish an area mismatch from a missing advertised LAN.
A Full neighbor does not guarantee that every required LAN is being advertised.

title: Secure a dual-stack VLAN gateway
summary: Repair an IPv6 VLAN gateway and isolate guest IPv6 traffic with a logical-interface ACL.
description: The switch trunk and both IPv4 VLAN gateways are already correct. VLAN gateway eth0.20 has an incorrect IPv6 address: replace it with 2001:db8:61::1/64. GUEST_V6 has the correct ordered rules: deny IPv6 from 2001:db8:61::/64 to 2001:db8:60::/64, then permit ip any any, but it is not bound. Apply GUEST_V6 IPv6 inbound on eth0.20. Guest must reach its own IPv6 gateway but must not reach Staff over ICMPv6, TCP 80 or UDP 53. Keep Guest-to-Staff IPv4 working, and keep Staff IPv6 gateway access working. Do not change the switch, client addresses or VLAN membership. IPv4 is deliberately permitted in this exercise.
hints: Configure IPv6 on the logical subinterface, not the physical trunk parent.
An IPv6 ACL does not filter IPv4. The guest gateway address belongs to the guest prefix, so the staff-prefix deny should not block it.
